title: When to take a Nile cruise
standfirst: Nile cruises sail all year, but the weather, the crowds and the prices change a great deal with the season. Here is how the year divides. This is part of our [[up]].

sections.heading: October to April: the cooler season
paragraphs: Days are warm and nights can be cool, especially in December and January. This is the busiest time, with the highest prices, particularly over Christmas, New Year and Easter.

sections.heading: May to September: the hot season
paragraphs: Temperatures in Luxor and Aswan are very high in summer. Sightseeing starts very early and the hottest hours are spent on board. Ships are quieter and prices are lower.

sections.heading: Busy dates
paragraphs: Christmas and New Year are the busiest and most expensive weeks. Prices and payment deadlines differ for these dates, and cabins sell out early.

sections.heading: Water levels and the lock
paragraphs: The lock at Esna is occasionally closed for maintenance, usually for a short period announced in advance. Cruises that run then may start or end at Esna, with the journey to Luxor by road.

faqs.q: Which month suits a Nile cruise?
faqs.a: For mild weather, November to February. For fewer crowds and lower prices, the shoulder months of October, March and April.

faqs.q: Is a Nile cruise in summer a good idea?
faqs.a: If you travel early in the day and rest at midday, yes. It is hot, but quieter and cheaper.
